tagline.text: An industrial and waterfall city in northern Mindanao with more than 20 waterfalls

location.label: Location
location.text: Iligan City, Lanao del Norte (about 90 minutes west of Cagayan de Oro)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May dry season (waterfalls are fuller in the rainy season, but trails are slippery)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–2,500 (one day, covering entrance to 2–3 waterfalls, motorcycle taxis and meals, airfare not included)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Laguindingan Airport (CGY, shared with Cagayan de Oro)

children.text: Iligan, known as the "City of Majestic Waterfalls," is a city in Lanao del Norte with more than 20 waterfalls scattered within roughly 30 km. You can combine Maria Cristina Falls, Tinago Falls and Mimbalut Falls in a day, and adding Timoga Spring, Bayug Island and Centennial Park makes a two-day trip.

Iligan sits on Iligan Bay on the north coast of Mindanao and, according to Wikipedia, had about 368,000 residents in 2024 and covers about 813 sq km. Its nicknames are "The Industrial Center of the South" and "City of Majestic Waterfalls." The two are linked: the water running through the city has long underpinned hydropower and the siting of factories. A good example is the Agus VI hydroelectric plant above Maria Cristina Falls, built by the National Power Corporation (NPC) in the early 1950s (commissioned May 1953) and described as still a main source of the city's power.

Guidebooks and local tourism guides say there are more than 20 waterfalls within about 30 km of Iligan. The best known is Maria Cristina Falls, followed by Tinago Falls, reached down a forest staircase, and Mimbalut Falls with its pool. Limunsudan Falls in Barangay Rogongon, about 50 km from the city, is described as the tallest waterfall in the Philippines (about 265 m, a claim Wikipedia flags as needing a citation), but it is closer to a multi-day expedition and not a typical tourist stop.

The city's history is said to begin on Bayug Island. Wikipedia explains that the first settlers here were the Higaonon Manobo and that Bayug Island lies in Barangay Hinaplanon, about 4 km north of the city center. Today's Iligan is home to Lumad, Moro, Visayan, Chavacano-speaking and other groups, and the festival honoring St. Michael is described as involving all of them. St. Michael's Cathedral stands downtown, and the Macaraeg-Macapagal ancestral house, described as the home of President Macapagal and his daughter, also stands by the national road in the city.

The most common way to see Iligan is a route that takes in a few waterfalls in a day. Local guides advise that more than three in a day is tiring, and say three days covers most of the sights. Motorcycle taxis called habal-habal are the easiest way between falls, and in town you use jeepneys and tricycles. However, entrance fees and operating status differ between guides, so check with the city tourism office or on site. In particular, a February 2026 visitor review said Maria Cristina Falls was not open to the public, so confirm whether it is open first.

The Agus River plunges over these falls, which one guide gives as about 340 feet (about 100 m) high. They lie within the NPC's Agus 6 hydroelectric complex, and a 10-hectare "NPC Nature's Park" opened in July 2010 so visitors could see the falls. The 2022 guide gave an adult entrance fee of about ₱35 and hours of 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., but a 2026 review said it was not open, so check the latest status.

This waterfall hides in a deep forest ravine, reached by going down a staircase described as 300 to 500 steps. Water falling from a cliff of about 240 feet forms a blue pool, and swimming and bamboo raft rides are popular. The 2022 guide gave an entrance fee of about ₱30, life vest rental at about ₱10–20 and cottage rental at about ₱100–300. Some visitors report guides or motorcycle drivers asking excessive fees, so agree on prices beforehand.

A waterfall in Barangay Buru-un, part of the Iligan Paradise Resort and Eco Park, about 500 m from the road and about 10 km from the city center. It is described as about 90 feet (about 27 m) high, and white water fanning over a wide rock slope makes it good for photos. The entrance fee varies from ₱15 to ₱50 depending on the guide.

A spring-fed swimming area in the Timoga area of Buru-un, with clear cold water, cottages and snack stalls, well suited to family picnics. The 2022 guide gave an entrance fee of about ₱50 and hours of 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., and mentions stalls selling roast pork.

Barangay Hindang is described as having a two-tiered waterfall about 12 m high with a swimming pool, plus a cluster of 6–8 caves. You can continue straight from the falls to cave exploring, which suits adventurous travelers. No exact hours or fees are given, so check on site.

A small island in the sea about 3.7–4 km northeast of the city center, said to be the home of the Higaonon Manobo who first settled this city. As a sitio of Barangay Hinaplanon, it offers a coastal village and views of Iligan Bay.

blocks.title: Centennial Park and St. Michael's Cathedral

children.text: Centennial Park is a free park open from 8 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., good for an evening stroll. St. Michael's Cathedral downtown is dedicated to the city's patron saint and is linked to the festival honoring St. Michael.
Buhanginan Hill, on the city hall grounds, is a viewpoint over the city, and Mount Agad-Agad at about 490 m above sea level is described as a spot for easy hiking and camping.
Have breakfast in town and head toward Buru-un by jeepney or motorcycle taxi. Agree on a full-day hire fare with the habal-habal driver before you get on.
Start with Mimbalut Falls. It is about a 500 m walk from the road, and the early hours are less crowded.
Go on to Tinago Falls, walk down the stairs and swim or take a raft ride in the pool. You have to climb back up, so keep some energy in reserve.
Return toward town and have lunch.
If Maria Cristina Falls is open, see the falls at NPC Nature's Park. If it is closed, switch to Centennial Park or Timoga Spring.
Take an evening stroll in Centennial Park, then have dinner at a restaurant in town.
More than three stops in one go is tiring, so three waterfalls is the best maximum.
Follow the one-day waterfall route above.
Swim at Timoga Spring and see Hindang Falls and its caves.
See St. Michael's Cathedral and the Macaraeg-Macapagal house in town, then relax on the coast toward Bayug Island.
Have an early dinner in town and take a bus to Cagayan de Oro.

Lodging is concentrated in the Pala-o, Mahayahay and Tubod districts of town. The 2022 guide lists Go Hotels Iligan in the Robinsons Place complex, Rene's Pension House on Roxas Avenue (from ₱350 for two) and The Loft Hotel, and says large hotels are few and budget rooms start in the ₱300 range. Wikivoyage also lists budget prices such as Famous Pension House at ₱450, but they may be out of date, so confirm before booking.

For food, guides mention Tita Fannie's for roast pork liempo and chicken, Jacko's Kan-Anan for Filipino home cooking, and El Canto Grill for seafood and sizzling dishes. Souvenirs include Cheding's peanuts and Pinakurat vinegar from Pala-o, and durian stalls along the road are common.
Waterfall operating status changes, so confirm in particular whether Maria Cristina Falls is open before you go.
The stairs at Tinago Falls are long and the climb back takes effort, so go early in the morning and bring water and a towel.
Agree on the price with habal-habal drivers and guides before you ride, and tell them how long you will hire them.
When swimming in a falls pool, rent a life vest, and do not enter the water when it rises in the rainy season.
More than three stops at once is tiring, so limit yourself to three waterfalls a day.
Waterfall entrance fees and habal-habal are often paid in cash, so carry plenty of small change.
You can visit Iligan as a day trip from Cagayan de Oro, but we recommend one night to see the waterfalls at a relaxed pace.
A February 2026 visitor review says Maria Cristina Falls was closed, so be sure to confirm whether it is open before you visit.
Before traveling, including to nearby areas such as Lanao del Sur toward Marawi, check the latest travel advisories from your foreign ministry and the Philippine Department of Tourism (DOT).
Waterfall pools and stairs are slippery in rain and dangerous when the water rises, so avoid swimming in the rainy season.
There are reports of motorcycle drivers and guides at Tinago Falls and elsewhere asking excessive fees, so agree on the price first.
Limunsudan Falls is a multi-day trek, so do not go without a guide, and ask the city tourism office whether access is possible.
Entrance fees and hours differ between guides, so follow the notices on site.
